CN.take: China's parcel leaders are trading volume for price: under anti-involution discipline ZTO lifted core ASP 15.5% on 6.5% more parcels and YTO grew profit 73% on 8% more revenue, while SF's volumes went negative in Q2. Growth has moved offshore and into returns, with SF's international express up 60%, AliExpress profitable on logistics optimisation and PDD warning that EU duties on low-value parcels push Temu towards local warehouses. For Western posts and cross-border operators we read this as fewer small direct parcels from China and more pre-positioned, bulk-imported stock.

AS.take: Southeast Asia is where parcel volume is growing fastest: J&T's regional volumes rose 71% and Shopee's orders 27.5%, while Japan's incumbents are shrinking volume and repairing margin through price. Growth is being paid for, as Sea's EBITDA rose 11% on 48% more revenue and Delhivery's margin fell while absorbing Ecom Express. Japan Post's domestic logistics slipped into loss as mail fell 5.9%, which we read as a warning that e-commerce parcels no longer offset letter decline for posts without pricing power.

highlights: Southeast Asia parcels +71.2% to 5.52bn; market share about 38%

companies.outlook: 2026 capex of US$800m to US$900m on sorting automation, vehicles and IT; buyback raised to HK$2.0bn.
companies.exposure: Southeast Asian parcel growth drove the profit jump, the intra-regional surge at the heart of ASEAN's digital rulebook.
